title: Overload — Tool Stalled
shortDescription: The M18/M12 tool has drawn excessive current and shut down to protect the motor.
fullDescription:
Milwaukee brushless tools (M18 Fuel, M12 Fuel, MX Fuel) use current sensing on the motor drive to protect the stator windings. E01 corresponds to 3 red LED flashes on the fuel gauge — the tool was stalled (bit bound, impact under excess torque, saw pinched). The tool locks out for a few seconds, then rearms.

Frequent E01 trips shorten brush (legacy) or bearing life and stress the driver circuit. Use the correct tool for the job.

causes.cause: Bit or blade bound in material

fixSteps.title: Release trigger
fixSteps.instruction: Let go of trigger for 3-5 seconds so the controller resets.

fixSteps.title: Free the bit
fixSteps.instruction: Back the bit out; check for dull/damaged bit.

fixSteps.title: Check battery
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in a freshly charged pack; low voltage sag triggers E01 faster.

whenToCallPro: If E01 trips on light work, send the tool to a Milwaukee service center — the drive board may be compromised.

faq.a: Occasional trips are normal and safe. Frequent overloads reduce tool life.

title: Tool Over-Temperature
shortDescription: Motor or electronics temperature too high — cool-down required.
fullDescription: Heavy continuous use heats the stator and driver MOSFETs. When internal temp exceeds ~80 °C the tool shuts down and displays E02 (solid red fuel gauge). Cool-down typically takes 10-20 minutes depending on ambient temperature.

causes.cause: Prolonged continuous use under heavy load

fixSteps.title: Let tool cool
fixSteps.instruction: Set in shade for 15-20 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Blow dust from cooling slots with compressed air.

whenToCallPro: If the tool runs hot with no heavy load, send for service — thermal sensor or MOSFETs may be failing.

faq.q: Can I dunk the tool in cold water?
faq.a: Never — it destroys the electronics. Air-cool only.

title: Battery Voltage Low
shortDescription: Battery voltage dropped below cut-off under load.
fullDescription:
E03 is posted when pack voltage sags below 15 V (M18) or 9 V (M12) during a load pulse. The cell BMS blocks further discharge to prevent damage.

On low-capacity packs (CP1.5, XC2.0), heavy impact work at <30% charge causes E03 frequently. Use HO/Forge packs for sustained heavy tools.

causes.cause: Cold battery (voltage sag in freezing weather)

fixSteps.title: Recharge or swap pack
fixSteps.instruction: Install a charged HO/Forge pack if available.

fixSteps.title: Warm cold pack
fixSteps.instruction: Let pack reach 10 °C+ before heavy use in winter.

affectedModels: Any M18/M12 tool with CP or XC pack
videoSearchQuery: Milwaukee battery cuts out low voltage

faq.q: Why does it happen with a full pack?
faq.a: Likely a weak cell in the pack — load capacity dropped even though resting voltage reads full.

title: Battery Communication Fault
shortDescription: Tool cannot read data from the M18/M12 battery pack.
fullDescription: Fuel packs communicate temperature, voltage, and state-of-charge to the tool over a data pin. E04 flags corrupted or missing data. Usually it is contamination on the terminal block; sometimes it is a failed BMS.
symptoms: Tool won't run with specific pack
Tool works fine with another pack

fixSteps.title: Clean terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe battery terminals with contact cleaner and a lint-free cloth.

fixSteps.title: Try another pack
fixSteps.instruction: If the tool runs with a different pack, the original pack is at fault.

fixSteps.title: Return pack
fixSteps.instruction: Milwaukee offers a 5-year battery warranty — contact support.

affectedModels: Any M18 Fuel / M12 Fuel tool with older Redlithium pack
whenToCallPro: Warranty-return the pack via Milwaukee support.
videoSearchQuery: Milwaukee battery data pin communication error

faq.a: Not officially — warranty replacement is the path.

title: Trigger Switch Stuck
shortDescription: Trigger reading non-zero with no input — tool disabled.
fullDescription: E05 appears when the variable-speed trigger potentiometer sends a non-zero signal at rest. Usually due to sawdust or concrete slurry contaminating the trigger assembly.

fixSteps.title: Blow out trigger
fixSteps.instruction: Press trigger fully and blow compressed air into the assembly; release and repeat.

fixSteps.title: Service trigger
fixSteps.instruction: If persistent, send to Milwaukee service center — trigger assemblies are not user-serviceable.

whenToCallPro: Trigger replacement requires handle disassembly — service center recommended.

faq.a: No — oil attracts more dust. Dry compressed air only.

title: Motor Hall Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Brushless motor position sensor reading invalid.
fullDescription:
Brushless Milwaukee motors use three Hall-effect sensors to commutate phases. E06 (persistent red + tool won't spin) means one or more sensors are failing — usually due to water/dust ingress after heavy outdoor use.

Field repair is not practical; send to service.

fixSteps.title: Confirm battery good
fixSteps.instruction: Try another pack to rule out battery.

fixSteps.title: Send for service
fixSteps.instruction: Motor replacement is done at a Milwaukee service center.

whenToCallPro: Always — motor swap requires balancing and firmware recognition.

faq.a: M18 Fuel carries a 5-year warranty. Keep purchase records.

title: One-Key Bluetooth Lockout
shortDescription: Tool has been remotely locked through Milwaukee One-Key.
fullDescription:
One-Key equipped tools can be disabled remotely. E07 appears when the owner's app has flagged the tool as locked — either as an anti-theft measure or to enforce a customized power profile.

Unlock from the Milwaukee One-Key app. If the owner no longer has the pairing, contact Milwaukee support with proof of purchase.

fixSteps.title: Open One-Key app
fixSteps.instruction: Launch app, find the tool in inventory, select Unlock.

fixSteps.title: Recover ownership
fixSteps.instruction: If locked by previous owner, call Milwaukee support with proof of purchase.

affectedModels: Any One-Key enabled M18 tool (2867, 2872, 2874, etc.)
whenToCallPro: Contact Milwaukee support for ownership disputes.

faq.a: Only Milwaukee can remove One-Key ownership after lock.

title: Charger Fault — Red/Green Flash
shortDescription: M18 Super Charger or M12/M18 Rapid Charger unable to charge pack.
fullDescription: Alternating red/green flashing on the charger corresponds to E08 — the charger has detected an abnormal pack condition and is refusing to charge. Causes include over-temp pack, under-voltage cell, or communication mismatch.

causes.cause: Pack too hot or too cold

fixSteps.title: Temperature conditioning
fixSteps.instruction: Remove pack from charger, let reach room temperature (15-30 min).

fixSteps.title: Try charge again
fixSteps.instruction: Return pack to charger — Super Charger has recovery mode for deep-discharged packs.

whenToCallPro: If pack refuses charge after conditioning, warranty replacement via Milwaukee.

faq.q: Can I jumpstart a dead pack?
faq.a: Never — this can cause a fire. Use only Milwaukee chargers.

title: Torque Sensor Fault (Impact/Wrench)
shortDescription: M18 Fuel impact wrench torque-control feedback lost.
fullDescription: Premium Milwaukee impact wrenches (2767-22, 2967-22) use a torque-feedback sensor for the precision mode. E09 indicates the sensor signal has gone out of range. Precision mode is disabled; max torque remains available.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Connect to One-Key app and install latest firmware; sometimes a software glitch causes E09.

fixSteps.title: Service center
fixSteps.instruction: Bring to Milwaukee service for sensor replacement.

whenToCallPro: Always — internal sensor access requires full disassembly.

faq.a: Yes at max torque, but precision mode is lost until repaired.

title: Chuck / Collet Slip
shortDescription: Bit slipping in chuck — not an electronic fault but a common warranty call.
fullDescription: Not a true error code but logged as E10 in diagnostic. Chuck jaws worn or contaminated; or a 1/4" hex shank worn at the retention ring. Replace worn chuck with OEM.
symptoms: Bit spins free of chuck under load

fixSteps.title: Retighten chuck
fixSteps.instruction: Firmly tighten keyless chuck — spin tool in reverse briefly to seat jaws.

fixSteps.title: Replace chuck
fixSteps.instruction: Remove chuck retention screw (left-hand thread), unscrew chuck with hex key in jaws.

faq.a: M18 Fuel drills use all-metal chucks; keep jaws clean for full grip.

title: Vibration Sensor Lockout (Grinder)
shortDescription: M18 Fuel grinder detected wheel imbalance — stopped for safety.
fullDescription: M18 Fuel grinders (2881-20, 2980-20) include a vibration sensor that stops the wheel if an unbalanced or damaged disc is detected — protecting the user from wheel rupture. E11 indicates this protection triggered.
symptoms: Grinder stops after 1-2 seconds of startup

fixSteps.title: Replace wheel
fixSteps.instruction: Install a fresh ANSI B7.1-rated wheel, ensuring correct flange orientation.

fixSteps.title: Check spindle
fixSteps.instruction: Spin spindle by hand — any roughness means bearings need service.

whenToCallPro: Spindle bearing service is a service-center job.

faq.a: No — the sensor protects you from wheel rupture at 9000+ RPM.

title: Anti-Kickback Stop (Circular Saw / Chainsaw)
shortDescription: Sudden deceleration detected — tool stopped to prevent kickback injury.
fullDescription:
M18 Fuel rear-handle saw (2830) and chainsaws have an Auto-Stop feature that kills the motor if the blade decelerates abnormally fast (pinched blade or chain snag). E12 is logged when this fires.

Release the trigger and pull the tool free before restarting.

fixSteps.title: Release trigger
fixSteps.instruction: Let go and back the saw out of the kerf.

fixSteps.title: Support workpiece
fixSteps.instruction: Use wedges to keep the kerf open; cut from both sides if necessary.

fixSteps.title: Inspect blade
fixSteps.instruction: Check for bent/damaged teeth; replace blade if damaged.

whenToCallPro: Only if E12 fires without a kickback event.

faq.a: No — it is a core safety feature.
